Progress toward badges ('3 of 5') drives engagement. Rules must be backfillable for historical actions.
topics.data_idea: Replays seeded user action histories, verifying badges grant exactly when criteria are met, once each.
topics.real_world_use: Stack Overflow badges, Duolingo achievements, and GitHub achievements run rule-based grant engines.

topics.name: Referral Code Tracker
topics.concept: Referral programs attribute signups: the tracker issues per-user codes, attributes new signups via code or cookie with a lookback window, and credits rewards after fraud checks (self-referral, duplicate devices). Leaderboards of top referrers add virality. Fraud rules are what keep the program solvent.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded signup flows with fraud attempts, verifying attribution and reward gating.
topics.real_world_use: Dropbox, Uber, and fintech referral programs attribute via codes with fraud checks.

topics.name: Affiliate Click Attributor
topics.concept: Affiliate marketing pays for driven sales: the attributor logs clicks with affiliate ids, attributes purchases within the cookie window (last-click usually wins), and splits commissions on multi-touch per policy. It handles returns by clawing back commissions. Accurate attribution is the money.
topics.data_idea: Replays seeded click/purchase/return streams, verifying attribution and commission math including clawbacks.
topics.real_world_use: Amazon Associates, ShareASale, and SaaS affiliate programs attribute and pay commissions this way.

topics.name: UTM Campaign Parser
topics.concept: Marketing attribution starts with UTM tags: the parser extracts utm_source/medium/campaign from URLs, normalizes naming conventions, attributes sessions to campaigns, and reports spend efficiency per campaign. Consistent taxonomy is enforced because 'Email' vs 'email' splits reports. It is unglamorous and essential.

key_params.attribution: first vs last touch session credit

topics.data_idea: Parses seeded URLs with messy UTM variants, verifying normalization and campaign rollup correctness.
topics.real_world_use: Every marketing team (HubSpot, Marketo users) standardizes UTMs for campaign ROI reporting.

topics.name: Cookie Consent Manager
topics.concept: Privacy law requires consent before tracking: the manager shows a banner, records granular choices (necessary, analytics, marketing), blocks non-essential scripts until consent, and stores proof of consent per user. Consent must be revocable and re-prompted on policy change. The audit trail is the legal artifact.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded visitor consent flows (accept, reject, granular, revoke) verifying script gating and receipt records.
topics.real_world_use: OneTrust, Cookiebot, and every EU-facing site implement consent banners with audit trails.

topics.name: Privacy Data Export Tool
topics.concept: Data-portability law lets users download their data: the export tool collects a user's records across services, packages them in machine-readable formats, and delivers a secure expiring download. It must include everything, exclude others' data, and complete within legal deadlines. Completeness is the compliance risk.
topics.data_idea: Exports seeded multi-service user datasets, verifying completeness, others'-data exclusion, and format validity.
topics.real_world_use: Google Takeout, Apple Data & Privacy, and GDPR Article 20 exports all package user data portably.

topics.name: Data Retention Sweeper
topics.concept: Retention policies say how long data lives: the sweeper applies per-category TTLs (logs 90 days, sessions 30), deletes or anonymizes expired rows in batches, and logs proof of deletion for audits. Legal holds pause deletion for litigation. Batch sizing keeps deletes from locking tables.
topics.data_idea: Ages seeded datasets past their TTLs, verifying correct rows are deleted/anonymized and holds are respected.
topics.real_world_use: Healthcare (HIPAA), finance, and GDPR storage-limitation compliance all run retention sweeping.

topics.name: Audit Log Service
topics.concept: Audit logs answer 'who did what when': the service appends immutable, tamper-evident records (hash-chained) of sensitive actions with actor, action, target, and before/after values. Retention and restricted read access complete it. Hash chaining makes silent tampering detectable.
topics.data_idea: Replays seeded admin actions (including a tamper attempt) verifying chain integrity detection and complete records.
topics.real_world_use: SOC 2, HIPAA, and financial regulators require tamper-evident audit trails (AWS CloudTrail model).

topics.name: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
topics.concept: RBAC manages permissions through roles: users get roles, roles get permissions, and checks ask 'does this user have permission X'. Role hierarchies and separation-of-duties constraints (no single user may both request and approve) encode policy. Reviews prune stale grants. It scales where per-user ACLs collapse.
topics.data_idea: Evaluates seeded users, roles, and requests, verifying allow/deny decisions and SoD enforcement.
topics.real_world_use: AWS IAM, Kubernetes RBAC, and enterprise apps all authorize through roles.

topics.name: Attribute-Based Policy Engine
topics.concept: ABAC decides with attributes, not just roles: policies combine user, resource, action, and context attributes ('managers can approve expenses under 5k in their department'). The engine evaluates policy sets with deny-overrides combining. It is more expressive than RBAC and harder to audit, so policy simulation matters.
topics.data_idea: Evaluates seeded requests against policies, verifying decisions and testing policy changes in simulation before deploy.
topics.real_world_use: AWS IAM policies, OPA/Rego, and Google Zanzibar-style systems evaluate attribute-based policies.

topics.name: API Scope Enforcer
topics.concept: OAuth scopes limit what a token can do: the enforcer maps endpoints to required scopes, checks the token's scope set per request, and returns 403 with insufficient-scope hints. Scope design (coarse vs fine) trades security against developer friction. It is authorization at the API boundary.
topics.data_idea: Sends seeded requests with various token scopes, verifying each endpoint enforces exactly its required scopes.
topics.real_world_use: GitHub, Google, and Slack APIs all gate endpoints on OAuth scopes.

topics.name: Tenant Isolation Middleware
topics.concept: Multi-tenant SaaS serves many customers from one deployment: the middleware resolves the tenant from subdomain, header, or token, scopes every query to the tenant id, and blocks cross-tenant access even on bugs. Row-level scoping plus connection-pool hygiene prevents leaks. A single missing WHERE tenant_id is a breach.

key_params.resolution: subdomain vs header vs token tenant id

topics.data_idea: Runs seeded multi-tenant request streams, verifying strict data separation including adversarial missing-scope attempts.
topics.real_world_use: Salesforce, HubSpot, and every B2B SaaS isolate tenants; the middleware is the enforcement point.

topics.name: Subdomain Router
topics.concept: Subdomains route to tenants or services: the router parses the host, matches wildcard patterns (*.app.example.com), and dispatches to tenant contexts or service handlers. It handles apex domains, reserved subdomains (www, api), and TLS certificate matching. Correct parsing must survive punycode and port suffixes.
topics.data_idea: Routes seeded Host headers (wildcards, apex, punycode, ports) verifying correct tenant/service dispatch.
topics.real_world_use: SaaS tenant subdomains (acme.app.com), GitHub Pages, and Vercel preview URLs all route on subdomains.

topics.name: White-Label Theme Service
topics.concept: White-label products reskin per customer: the theme service resolves the tenant's brand (colors, logos, fonts, copy overrides), serves themed assets with caching, and falls back to defaults for missing keys. Theme validation keeps contrast accessible. It lets one codebase wear many brands.
topics.data_idea: Resolves seeded tenant themes (complete, partial, missing) verifying fallback correctness and asset URLs.
topics.real_world_use: Agency platforms, franchise software, and embedded fintech (banking-as-a-service) white-label per client.

topics.name: Maintenance Mode Middleware
topics.concept: Deploys and incidents need a maintenance page: the middleware flips a flag (config, file, or env), serves 503 with Retry-After to all traffic except allowlisted IPs, and shows a branded status page. Health checks stay green so orchestrators do not kill the instance mid-maintenance. Fast flip-off matters as much as on.
topics.data_idea: Toggles maintenance under seeded traffic, verifying 503s, allowlist bypass, and health-check exemption.
topics.real_world_use: Rails maintenance pages, Vercel, and status-page integrations all gate traffic during deploys.

topics.name: Deploy Preview Router
topics.concept: Preview deployments give every pull request a live URL: the router maps branch-based subdomains to ephemeral environments, tears them down on merge, and protects them with auth. Routing must isolate preview traffic from production data. It shortens review cycles from days to minutes.
topics.data_idea: Routes seeded branch deployments through create/preview/merge/teardown, verifying isolation and cleanup.
topics.real_world_use: Vercel, Netlify, and Railway preview deployments spin per-PR environments with branch URLs.

topics.name: Blue-Green Traffic Splitter
topics.concept: Blue-green deploys run two environments and switch traffic: the splitter shifts percentages from blue to green, monitors error rates during the shift, and auto-rolls back on regression. Sticky sessions drain gracefully. Instant rollback is the payoff for the doubled capacity cost.
topics.data_idea: Shifts seeded traffic with injected green regressions, verifying ramp progression and automatic rollback.
topics.real_world_use: AWS CodeDeploy, Spinnaker, and Kubernetes progressive delivery all shift traffic with guardrails.

topics.name: Request Coalescing (Singleflight)
topics.concept: When a cache entry expires, hundreds of concurrent requests can stampede the backend recomputing it: singleflight coalescing lets the first request do the work while the rest wait on the same in-flight call and share its result. The registry keys in-flight calls, attaches waiters, and propagates errors or cancellations to all of them. It turns a thundering herd into one backend call.

key_params.key_fn: how requests are grouped into one flight
key_params.timeout: max wait before waiters give up

topics.data_idea: Fires seeded concurrent request bursts at expiring cache keys and verifies backend call counts collapse to one per key with all waiters served.
topics.real_world_use: Go's singleflight, GraphQL dataloaders, and CDN origin shields coalesce duplicate in-flight requests.

topics.name: Signed URL Generator (Presigned URLs)
topics.concept: Presigned URLs grant time-limited access to private objects without proxying bytes: the server signs the object key, expiry, and allowed method with HMAC, and the storage backend verifies the signature on arrival. The generator sets content-disposition and content-type constraints inside the signature so they cannot be tampered with. Leaked URLs simply expire.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded signed URLs (valid, expired, tampered) and verifies the verifier accepts only genuine unexpired ones with constraints honored.
topics.real_world_use: S3 presigned URLs, Google Cloud signed URLs, and private file downloads all use HMAC-signed time-limited URLs.

topics.name: JSON:API Relationship Expander
topics.concept: JSON:API standardizes compound documents: primary data plus an included section with related resources, sparse fieldsets limiting attributes, and links for pagination. The expander resolves relationship paths, dedupes included resources by type+id, and applies fieldset filtering. It eliminates both over-fetching and N+1 client round trips.

key_params.dedupe: included-section dedupe by type and id

topics.data_idea: Builds seeded resource graphs and verifies compound documents contain exactly the requested relationships with no duplicates.
topics.real_world_use: JSON:API backends (Ember Data, some Rails APIs) standardize compound documents and sparse fieldsets.

topics.name: Content-Addressable Asset Store
topics.concept: Content addressing names files by their hash: identical content dedupes automatically, and the hash doubles as an integrity check on every read. The store shards blobs by hash prefix, serves them with immutable cache headers, and garbage-collects unreferenced blobs. It is how CDNs and caches get infinite cache lifetimes safely.
topics.data_idea: Stores seeded file sets with duplicates and verifies dedupe ratios, hash integrity on read, and immutable caching headers.
topics.real_world_use: Git objects, Docker layers, IPFS, and CDN hashed-asset pipelines all address content by hash.

topics.name: GraphQL Query Planner (Lite)
topics.concept: GraphQL lets clients ask for exactly the fields they need: the planner parses queries into an AST, validates them against the schema (types, arguments, depth limits), and plans batched resolver execution to avoid N+1 fetches. Query complexity scoring rejects abusive queries before execution. The planner is what makes 'ask for anything' safe.
topics.data_idea: Executes seeded queries (valid, too-deep, over-complex, N+1-prone) verifying validation rejects and batching collapses fetches.
topics.real_world_use: Apollo Server, Hasura, and GitHub's GraphQL API parse, validate, and plan queries with complexity limits.

topics.name: Edge Request Mutator (Edge Workers)
topics.concept: Edge workers run code at CDN points of presence before requests reach the origin: the mutator rewrites URLs, injects geo headers, runs A/B bucketing, and serves cached variants per segment. It executes in isolates with tight CPU limits, so the programming model is event-driven and stateless. Personalization moves from origin to edge.

key_params.limits: CPU and memory caps per invocation

topics.data_idea: Runs seeded requests through worker scripts, verifying rewrites, geo injection, and variant serving at simulated edge nodes.
topics.real_world_use: Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute, and AWS Lambda@Edge execute request mutation at the edge.

topics.name: Distributed Tracing Sampler
topics.concept: Tracing every request is too expensive, so samplers decide which traces to keep: head-based sampling decides at request start (fast, but misses interesting tails), tail-based sampling buffers and keeps traces with errors or high latency. The sampler propagates trace context (traceparent) across services either way. Sampling strategy determines what you can debug later.
topics.data_idea: Replays seeded multi-service traces with errors and verifies kept-trace sets match the strategy's intent within the budget.
topics.real_world_use: OpenTelemetry collectors, Jaeger, and Honeycomb implement head/tail sampling with context propagation.

topics.name: Shadow Traffic Mirroring
topics.concept: Shadow traffic duplicates production requests to a staging environment so new code proves itself on real traffic without affecting users: the mirror copies requests, strips PII, compares responses against production, and diffs divergences. Write requests get sandboxed so shadows never mutate real state. It catches bugs load tests miss.
topics.data_idea: Mirrors seeded production traffic to a candidate build, verifying PII scrubbing, write sandboxing, and divergence diffs.
topics.real_world_use: Diffy (Twitter), Goreplay, and Envoy traffic shadowing validate deploys against real production load.

topics.name: Backend-for-Frontend Request Aggregator
topics.concept: Mobile and web clients need different data shapes, so a BFF aggregates: one client call fans out to several microservices in parallel, and the aggregator merges, reshapes, and trims the responses into the exact payload the UI needs. Timeouts and partial-failure policies decide what the client sees when one service is slow. It trades backend chattiness for client simplicity.

key_params.partial: fail-whole vs degrade on partial failure

topics.data_idea: Fans seeded client requests out to fake services with random latencies/failures, verifying merged payloads and partial-failure behavior.
topics.real_world_use: SoundCloud, mobile BFFs, and GraphQL gateways all aggregate microservice responses per client.

topics.name: Double-Submit Cookie CSRF Defense
topics.concept: The double-submit pattern avoids server-side CSRF state: the server sets a random token in a cookie and the client must echo the same value in a header or form field, which a cross-site attacker cannot read due to the same-origin policy. Validation compares the two values in constant time. It pairs naturally with JWT-based stateless auth.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded cross-site posts with missing/mismatched pairs, verifying only requests with matching cookie-and-echo pass.
topics.real_world_use: Angular's XSRF-TOKEN cookie/header pair and stateless SPA backends use double-submit CSRF defense.

topics.name: WebSocket Backpressure Controller
topics.concept: Fast producers overwhelm slow consumers: the backpressure controller monitors per-connection send buffers, applies pause/resume signals or drops to best-effort for stale data, and sheds load by disconnecting the slowest consumers first. High/low watermarks prevent oscillation. Without it, one slow client can OOM the server.
topics.data_idea: Streams seeded producer/consumer pairs with mismatched speeds, verifying pause/resume engages and memory stays bounded.
topics.real_world_use: Socket.IO, MQTT brokers, and game servers all apply backpressure so slow clients cannot exhaust server memory.

topics.name: HTTP/3 QUIC Concept Simulator
topics.concept: QUIC rebuilds transport on UDP: independent streams eliminate head-of-line blocking, connection migration survives network switches, and TLS 1.3 is integrated into the handshake for faster setup. The simulator models streams multiplexed over one connection with per-stream flow control and packet-loss recovery. It shows why HTTP/3 helps lossy mobile networks most.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded transfers over lossy links for QUIC-like vs TCP-like transports, comparing completion times and stall behavior.
topics.real_world_use: Google, Cloudflare, and Meta serve HTTP/3 over QUIC; mobile apps benefit from connection migration.
